finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in the /dl handler lets any remote client read arbitrary files readable by the server process. The user-supplied query parameter f is joined onto root without stripping '..' or checking the resolved path stays under root.
finding.source: files.go:12 r.URL.Query().Get("f"), route registered at files.go:32, no auth
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); response body written at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken directly from query param f, no sanitization
filepath.Join lexically cleans '../../etc/passwd' to '/etc/passwd'; os.ReadFile reads it
file contents written to the HTTP response

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no '..' rejection, no Clean-then-prefix or filepath.Rel check against root, no authentication or authorization on /dl. Sibling handler avatar (files.go:22) applies filepath.Base, which blocks traversal; download lacks the equivalent control. avatar path (files.go:23) checked and SAFE: Base strips directories, and directory reads fail.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12-13 take the raw query value into filepath.Join(root, name) with no filepath.Base, no '..' rejection, and no prefix/filepath.Rel containment check. The /dl route (files.go:32) has no auth wrapper. Only the NotFound branch (files.go:14-16) exists and it does not gate reads. The avatar handler's filepath.Base (files.go:22) does not apply to download.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: files.go:12 reads f unsanitized, files.go:13 Join(root, "../../etc/passwd") lexically cleans to /etc/passwd and os.ReadFile reads it, files.go:18 writes the bytes to the response, and files.go:32 registers /dl with no authentication, so an anonymous remote client can read any file the server process can read.
